original_raw_record.support_text: Loss of ΔΨm in K562 cells treated with 6.0 µM Q39 for 6–48 h in hypoxia was assessed with JC-1 staining, indicated by a switch from red to green fluorescence. Compared with the corresponding control, Q39 decreased ΔΨm in K562 cells after 12–48 h incubation in a time-dependent manner. Quantitative flow cytometry showed the percentages of cells with low ΔΨm increased nearly 10-fold in cells exposed to Q39 for 48 h compared with the corresponding control in hypoxia.

original_raw_record.support_text: In the safety analysis of a study comparing IVCA (ivacaftor) therapy between a study group (SG) and observation group (OG), hepatotoxicity due to IVCA therapy occurred in two patients (2.1%) in the SG and one patient (1.1%) in the OG (p=0.62). One SG patient had raised ALT with bilirubin elevation (Naranjo score +5, probable); the remaining two patients (one SG, one OG) had raised alkaline phosphatase with accompanying gamma-glutamyl transferase elevation (Naranjo +5 probable and +3 possible, respectively).
original_raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Patients with diabetic foot infection treated with IVCA; one hepatotoxicity case occurred in the observation group (attribution to IVCA implied by the authors).
original_raw_record.extra_details: Three hepatotoxicity cases adjudicated with the Naranjo adverse-drug-reaction scale. SG case 1: raised ALT with bilirubin elevation (Naranjo +5, probable). SG case 2 and OG case: raised ALP with GGT elevation (Naranjo +5 probable and +3 possible, respectively). Hepatotoxicity rate 2.1% (2/94) SG vs 1.1% (1/95) OG, p=0.62. IVCA is used here for diabetic foot infection (DFI). No dose/schedule or liver-failure outcome reported in the provided window.
